sections.h2: Where does Van Buren County record a deed, and when can you go in?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and the other papers that touch Van Buren County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds, 219 E. Paw Paw Street, Suite 102, in Paw Paw, the county seat. The online records page lists office hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday except holidays, and the phone line is (269) 657-8242.

The county's about page says the office has existed since Michigan's first constitution in 1836 and handles more than 430 kinds of documents. Only originals with live signatures, or certified court documents, can be recorded. A photocopy or fax is turned away.

Staff check each paper against state requirements, scan it and return the original to whoever sent it in. Their FAQ promises recording and return within one to two days when the paper is in order. If a title company or attorney handles your closing, the original comes back to them first, so ask them when it will reach you.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Van Buren County counter?
sections.html:
One flat charge covers a deed or mortgage of any length. The county fee page prints the figures below, and the same amounts appear in MCL 600.2567.

Van Buren County Register of Deeds charges as printed on the county fee page
ItemAmountDetail from the page
Recording a deed, mortgage or other instrument$30.00Same price regardless of page count; $4.00 of it goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund
Extra instruments in one assignment or discharge$3.00 eachAdded for each instrument assigned or discharged
Copies$1.00 per pageFax, email or mail copies available
Certification$5.00 per documentApplies to certified copies
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00Can be included in the same payment

Recording and transfer tax payments are cash or check only, with checks made out to Register of Deeds. Credit cards work only for copies ordered online. When you mail a package, include a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return.

sections.h2: Which Van Buren County deeds need a treasurer's certificate before recording?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments that carry a warranty covenant need a tax certificate from the Van Buren County Treasurer before the Register of Deeds will take them. The county's fee page and its FAQ both say so, and the rule comes from MCL 211.135.

That statute asks for proof that all taxes on the parcel were paid for the five years before the date of the instrument. It also asks for a statement about tax liens or tax titles held against the land. A quitclaim deed with no covenants of warranty is excused from the certificate.

  • Order the certificate early; the recording office will not accept the deed without it.
  • Expect the $5.00 certificate fee on top of the $30.00 recording fee.
  • If back taxes show up, they are normally paid from your sale proceeds, so ask the treasurer for the balance before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax charged on a Van Buren County sale?
sections.html:
The seller or grantor owes it, provided the property value is $100.00 or more. The Van Buren page lists two layers: the county tax at $0.55 per $500 or fraction of $500, and the state tax at $3.75 per $500 or fraction. Those rates match MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

The deed must state the total consideration, or you attach a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, which costs nothing to file. For an exchange, each deed is taxed on the actual value of its property. If the land crosses a county line, state a sale price for each parcel and pay the tax in each county.

State law gives the seller 15 days after delivering the deed to pay the county treasurer (MCL 207.523). If a sale turns out to have been exempt, the state Treasury refund application must be filed within four years of payment, according to the county page.

Family transfers often qualify for relief. MCL 207.526 exempts these among others:

  • A deed from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child.
  • A deed from a grandparent to a grandchild.
  • A deed that confirms title the buyer already holds.
  • A court order that makes a transfer without a stated price.

sections.h2: What makes the Register of Deeds reject a Van Buren County document?
sections.html:
The office lists common errors itself: a wrong fee, a missing drafter's name, names that are handwritten instead of typed, and an incomplete notary certificate. Their requirements page tracks MCL 565.201.

  • Print or type each name under its signature, and make the printed names match the acknowledgment.
  • Show the addresses of all parties and the name and address of the person who drafted the document.
  • Leave a 2 1/2 inch blank top margin on page one and a half inch elsewhere, with type no smaller than 10 point.
  • Use sheets no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • For a deed that mentions a surviving owner, attach a certified death certificate.

The office does not draft documents or give legal advice. Ask an attorney, a title company or a real estate agent for help with the wording.

sections.h2: How can you look up a recorded deed in Van Buren County?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds site offers an online index at deeds.vanburencountymi.gov where you can search the records and buy images one document at a time. Copy orders placed online can take up to two working days, and the records site says large orders may need up to 48 hours. If you lack the liber and page, call the office. A BS&A property search also shows liber and page numbers in the legal description, plus a sale history.

Payment for older documents depends on the volume: liber 924 or lower is paid through the county's GovPayNow link, while liber 925 and higher is bought from the searchable index and downloads after payment. Anyone can get a copy of any recorded deed, since recorded papers are public.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Van Buren County itself?
sections.html:
Van Buren County covers 1,090 square miles, and 44 percent of that is Lake Michigan water. The county was created in 1829 and organized in 1837, and the seat is Paw Paw. Its cities are Bangor, Gobles, Hartford and part of South Haven, and villages include Decatur, Lawton, Mattawan and Lawrence. Much of the land is farmland and small towns, with lakeshore cottages and tourism near the water. Antwerp and Almena townships, next to Kalamazoo County, are drawing suburban growth.

I-94, I-196, US 31 and M-40 cross the county, and the Pere Marquette Amtrak line serves it. Michigan leaves zoning, building permits and assessing to cities and townships, so call the local township or city hall about a permit question.

The Census Bureau counts 76,071 residents in 2025, 30,622 households and an owner-occupancy rate of 80.6 percent for 2020 to 2024. The median owner-occupied home value is $206,500, median household income $68,114 and median gross rent $870. Density is about 124 people per square mile, so a lakefront cottage and a farm parcel are very different sales.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Van Buren County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30.00 per document regardless of page count, with $3.00 more for each extra instrument assigned or discharged. Certified copies and the treasurer's tax certificate are $5.00 each, and plain copies are $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Van Buren County Register of Deeds by card?
faqs.a: Not for recording. Recording and transfer tax are cash or check only, payable to Register of Deeds. Cards are accepted for copies bought online through the county's payment link.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when a Van Buren County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor pays, as long as the property value is $100.00 or more. The rates are $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, each counted by $500 or fraction of $500.

faqs.q: How long does recording take in Van Buren County?
faqs.a: The office says it records and returns a compliant document within one to two days of receipt. A paper with a wrong fee, missing drafter name or untyped names is rejected instead.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need a Van Buren County treasurer's certificate?
faqs.a: No. The certificate is required for warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments with a warranty covenant. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excused under MCL 211.135.
